title: Flow Off Main Thread Node Computation With Loading Chrome
description:
Node computation in the flow graph (flow_core FlowHost::evaluate_internal / touch_channel_eval) runs synchronously on whatever thread mutates the host. The React renderer's FlowGraphCanvasHost owns a main-thread FlowSession and calls loadFixtureJson/evaluateSync directly, so heavy evaluations (e.g. procedural-3d's "Sphere Cut With Torus" example, which drives brep.bool.cut -> boolean_mesh_sync, a ~20s WASM stall) freeze the UI. The procedural plugin worker also re-evaluates the whole graph synchronously on every action/render.

Goal: move all flow node computation off the main thread and show per-node loading chrome (the dag canvas already has unfed animated active/stale border chrome) while nodes compute. Verify on procedural-3d "Sphere Cut With Torus".

Approach (see approved plan): tick-driven evaluation inside the plugin worker via a budgeted evaluator (neural/engine), a shared FlowEvalDriver (flow/core), pending_effects wired through refreshUi/action responses using the existing HostEffect::DispatchAction self-dispatch loop, new NodeGraphScene.evalJson / World3dScene.statusJson fields, and renderer changes (React + wgpu) that stop evaluating locally and instead apply eval outputs + computing progress from the scene.

Full plan on disk at /Users/ueli/.claude/plans/flow-the-computation-of-sparkling-whale.md.
